claim: Slap Kozjak is a 15 m waterfall in a moss-walled cave-amphitheatre inside Triglav NP, accessed by a 45-minute walk from Kobarid town centre.
quote: Kozjak Waterfall (Slap Kozjak) is a 15-meter-high waterfall in Kobarid, in the Triglav National Park in Slovenia... it's located inside a cave, with walls covered in moss

claim: The Slap Kozjak out-and-back is 2.2 miles with ~456 ft elevation gain, averaging ~1 h 6 min; rated moderate; best May–September.
quote: 2.2-mile out-and-back route with an elevation gain of 456 feet. It takes an average of 1 hour 6 minutes... The best times to visit this trail are May through September

claim: Kozjak entry costs €5 adults / €3 children under 15, trail open 2 April – 31 October.
quote: the entrance fee to Slap Kozjak is €5 per person, with reduced prices of €3 for children under 15. The trail is open from April 2–October 31

claim: Tolmin Gorges (the lowest entry into Triglav National Park) charge tiered tickets, usually open April–October with advance online booking recommended.
quote: Tolmin Gorges are usually open from April to October

claim: A full Tolmin Gorges loop takes 1.5–2 hours and visits the Confluence, thermal spring, Bear's Head rock, Devil's Bridge and Dante's Cave; 2026 adult tickets run €8–€12 by season.
quote: Now, you are walking on an elevated path along the crystal clear, aquamarine water of the Tolminka River.

claim: Slap Boka is Slovenia's highest waterfall at 136 m (106 m free fall + 30 m), with a parking pull-off just off the Bovec–Kobarid road by the Boka bridge.
quote: Slap Boka is one of the highest and most powerful waterfalls in Slovenia, with a 136-meter height and 18-meter width. It begins with a 106-meter free fall, followed by another 30 meters

claim: The Boka viewpoint walk is ~15 minutes one-way and easy; reaching the source is a steep ~3.5 h technical scramble; flow is best in snowmelt spring and rainy autumn.
quote: The short and easy hike to the official Slap Boka viewpoint takes around 15 minutes... In spring and autumn, when the snow melts and rainfall increases, the Boka Waterfall is at its most impressive

claim: Slap Virje is a wide multi-stranded 12 m fall on the Glijun stream, 3.5 km from Bovec, reached by an easy 5-minute walk from a paid car park; no entry fee, parking €5.
quote: small but beautiful spot where water cascades over mossy rocks into an emerald green pool, located just 3.5km from the village of Bovec... There is no entrance fee at Slap Virje. The only fee is the parking one, which is 5€ for cars

claim: Velika korita Soče (the Great Soča Gorge) is a 750 m limestone canyon with pools up to 15 m deep, free to visit, ~10 minutes' drive from Bovec with roadside parking.
quote: The strait is about 750 m long, and its pools reach a depth of up to 15 m

claim: A popular linear walk links Mala korita to Velika korita Soče (~3.5 km one way, 1.5 h, easy, negligible elevation) with lookouts, swim spots and cliff-jumping access along the river.
quote: The hike length is 3.5 km one way (7 km total), takes 1.5 hours each way, is easy in difficulty, and has negligible elevation difference

claim: Kobarid's stone Napoleon Bridge over the Soča (first built 1750, blown up 1915, rebuilt) sits ~10 minutes' walk from town and is the gateway to the Slap Kozjak trail.
quote: The year 1750 is remembered as the moment when stone replaced wood... On 24 May 1915, retreating Austro-Hungarian troops blew up the old stone bridge

claim: The Mangart Saddle road climbs to 2,055 m – Slovenia's highest road – via 12 km of asphalt, 5 rock-cut tunnels and a 980 m climb, built in 1938.
quote: The Mangart Road is a narrow 12-kilometre long asphalt road that climbs 980 metres of altitude and goes through five tunnels carved into bedrocks. It was built in 1938

claim: Mangart road charges a €10 ecological toll, is typically open May–November, and has gradients up to 23 % – uphill traffic has priority on the narrow sections.
quote: One must pay an ecological tax of 10 € to drive on the road... The road is generally open from May through November

claim: Krnsko jezero, at 1,391 m, is Slovenia's largest high-mountain glacial lake (~400 m long, 17 m deep); swimming forbidden.
quote: Krnsko jezero lake is nearly 400 metres long, 150 metres wide and 17 metres deep in its deepest part, and lies at a height of 1,391 metres

claim: The standard Krn Lake hike starts from Dom dr. Klementa Juga in Lepena, gaining ~700 m on a zig-zag mule trail past Planinski dom pri Krnskih jezerih (~2 h up); summiting Mt Krn (2,244 m) adds ~3 h.
quote: follow a wide mule trail that zigzags across a steep slope covered with beech forest for almost two hours (~700 m altitude gain)... the hike to Mount Krn, for example, will take you another 3h hike to reach the top

claim: Šunikov vodni gaj in the Lepena valley is a short circular wooden-walkway trail through a 100 m emerald gorge cut by the Lepenjica and Šumnik streams.
quote: The Lepenjica and Šumnik streams create a 100 meters long and 10 meters deep emerald gorge

claim: The Šunik water-grove loop is ~3 km, takes 40–60 min, has no entry fee and is family-friendly with wooden boardwalks and rest stops.
quote: Visitors can take an approximately three-kilometer-long circular walk route. The loop trail is relatively short, taking about 40 minutes to 1 hour

claim: Vršič Pass (1,611 m) is Slovenia's highest paved pass with 50 hairpins; closed roughly late-October to early May due to avalanche risk; allow ~2 h to drive over with stops.
quote: the highest mountain pass in the country at 1,611m... 50 of them!... Expect it to take at least 2 hours to drive over the pass

claim: Mt Stol (1,673 m) above Kobarid is the highest peak of the long Julian Alps ridge with sea-to-Alps panoramic views, identifiable by its summit transmitter; multiple routes from Breginj or Kobarid via Veliki rob.
quote: Stol is the highest Slovenian peak in the longest ridge of the Julian Alps. It is an exceptional viewpoint from which you can see from the sea to the central Julian Alps

claim: Drežnica/Drežniške Ravne offer the classic western view of Mt Krn's wall and the southern Krn approach via Planina Kuhinja; Krasji vrh (1,773 m) from Drežniške Ravne is a 4–5 h, 9 km round trip with WWI ruins.
quote: The most beautiful view of the 2,244 meter-high Krn mountain is from Kobarid or Drežnica

claim: Slap Brinta (~104 m) and neighbouring Slap Gregorčičev (88 m) sit above Selce on the old Kobarid–Tolmin road via Kamno; a ~30-minute trail descends to the base but is unmaintained and risky in rain.
quote: Slap Brinta is a 104 meter high waterfall located near the town Selce... In heavy rain, the waterfall cannot be reached directly, as you simply cannot cross the river bed
